title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. A camera system flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, and that flag became the basis for a felony stop of two men in a different car. The failure happened in the field, at the moment the alert was acted on, not in the camera itself. The deputies who responded had no independent confirmation of the plate, and the undercover unit and helicopter could not read it either, so the stop rested on the alert alone.

Catching it would have required a verified plate match before weapons were drawn and men were handcuffed. The correction came only after the handcuffs were on, when deputies realized the car was not the stolen one. A check placed before the escalation rather than after it is the difference between a mistaken alert and an armed detention.

What is not established is whether department procedures were followed. That question is under review by supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants and shift sergeants, who will examine body worn camera footage. No charges were filed, the account of the stop comes from the two men, and the attorney their family plans to hire has not been retained.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
Harris County Sheriff's deputies in Cypress, Texas, mistook two men, both 19 years old, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves on Aug. 3. The men had just returned from a gas station, and Anthony was leaving in his Camaro when at least five patrol cars and a helicopter surrounded them. Deputies pointed guns, handcuffed them, and Julian said a deputy pushed him down, leaving cuts and scrapes. Deputies thought the car was stolen because flock cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, and an undercover unit and helicopter could not read the plates.

After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car and that the two were not suspects. They were not charged. Supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so. Anthony's mother, Leslie, said she plans to hire an attorney.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
